messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: 15 pods matching label pool=vllm-eu in namespace inference-prod are CrashLoopBackOff. Exit signal 11 (segfault) from /opt/runtime/bin/vllm-server. Restart backoff escalating. Autoscaler reports 3 node flaps in the last 10m. Pager escalated to oncall-ml.

maria: ack — I'm on it. any immediate customer-facing errors reported?

aj: seeing a flood of 503s from the HTTP ingress for the vllm route. Cloudwatch/metrics show 5xx spike aligned with the pods restarting. Support ticket #CS-4921 opened by Liz a few mins ago.

sre-anna: digging into the node logs now. dmesg on ip-10-0-7-45 shows a sequence: `NVRM: Xid 31, GPU access fault` followed by `kernel: task vllm-server:... killed as a result of fatal signal 11` — looks like GPU driver or illegal memory access. also a couple of `oom_kill_process` messages on other nodes.

aj: pod logs (tail) show immediate segfault during model load on some shards. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:15:22Z] loading model segment 0
[2026-03-15T02:15:22Z] nvrtc: compiling fused kernels
[2026-03-15T02:15:22Z] runtime error: Illegal instruction (core dumped)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
#0  0x7f9c1a2b in decode_kernel()
#1  0x7f9c1ac7 in load_model()
#2  0x400f3a in main
```

kevin: initial hypothesis: quantized/TensorRT fused kernels hitting an illegal memory instruction on certain sequence lengths or batch shapes. We saw a similar pattern with an earlier driver update but not this widespread. Did a system image or driver rollout happen recently?

infra-bot: No recent GPU driver upgrades in eu region in the last 24h. Noted a nodeset autoscaler activity 02:06Z that added 4 spots.

maria: mitigation options — quick ones: 1) move traffic to fallback model variant on CPU for impacted customer routes, 2) set env VLLM_DISABLE_FUSED=1 to disable fused kernels, 3) cordon & drain the 2 most flappy nodes to avoid scheduling on potentially corrupted host, 4) roll back to previous container image (v2.4.1) if this started after a runtime deploy.

aj: trying #2 now — patched k8s deployment inference/vllm-runtime: added env VLLM_DISABLE_FUSED=true and started a rolling restart. deploy-bot: starting rollout for vllm-runtime with env patch (strategy=RollingUpdate, maxUnavailable=2).

deploy-bot: rollout started. will report status.

sre-anna: cordoning ip-10-0-7-45 and ip-10-0-7-46; starting drain for one at a time. marking unschedulable.

kevin: also recommend setting pod memory limits slightly higher to avoid host OOM interplay while we debug: bump to 48Gi for heavy shards as stopgap.

aj: after env change rollout, observed 6 previously-crashing pods now running without segfault for ~40s. still seeing 4 pods crash (different nodes). logs from a crashing pod include driver message `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and a subsequent segfault.

maria: customer-impact: Liz — CS team reports 8 customers with degraded latency and increased 500s. One enterprise account (acct-855) reported realtime inference timeouts affecting live feature flags. CS contact updated with workaround: route to dedicated model via API gateway. ETA for full mitigation unknown.

aj: capturing core dump for one crashed pod to gcs: gs://redwood-incident-dumps/3124578901/pod-vllm-xyz/core-20260315.gz

sre-anna: collecting system traces: `nvidia-smi -q` shows ECC errors low, driver 525.89.10. NVML shows occasional timeout. Creating issue with ML runtime team.

kevin: quick repro steps I ran on staging replicate a crash when batch_size=64 + seq_len=8192 with quantized TRT path. disabling fused kernels avoids crash in staging. likely a kernel optimization bug in our fused op.

maria: previous deploy of vllm-runtime v2.5.0 went out ~01:50Z — timeline matches. rolling back to v2.4.1 might be safest if rollout with env var doesn't fully stabilize.

deploy-bot: rolling restart reported: 9/15 pods ready after patch; continuing.

aj: paging note — still seeing customer errors for ~10% of requests routed to the affected pool. recommend traffic shift for enterprise-tier customer routes to dedicated capacity immediately.

customer-success-liz: contacting affected customers with an interim note: we have partial mitigation in place (disabling fused kernels). offering dedicated capacity route as workaround. will update CS-4921.

maria: decision: 1) continue env-based rollout to disable fused kernels across vllm-runtime in eu, 2) cordon and drain suspect nodes, 3) open rollback PR to v2.4.1 as standby if rollouts don't finish within 20m, 4) notify customers via CS thread. assigning follow-ups: aj (runtime logs + core dumps), kevin (repro & root cause), sre-anna (nodes & infra), liz (customer comms).

aj: noted. collecting all crash traces and attaching to ticket INC-2026-032. core dumps available at the bucket above.

sre-anna: cordon/drain done for ip-10-0-7-45; no new pods scheduled there. monitoring.

deploy-bot: rollout completed: 15/15 pods restarted, env VLLM_DISABLE_FUSED=true applied.

aj: post-rollout status: crash rate dropped from 15->1 over the last 10m. still tracking one pod that fails intermittently — investigating persistent host level issue.

maria: handing off to night oncall (sre-anna) in 15m. summary for handoff: root cause suspected TRT/fused kernel illegal memory access triggered by certain seq_len+batch shapes after the v2.5.0 runtime deploy. mitigation applied (disabled fused kernels), cordoned flappy nodes, increased mem limits on heavy shards, core dumps uploaded. customer impact limited to degraded latency & 5xxs for ~8 customers; CS ticket updated. follow-ups: reproducer fix in runtime, investigate kernel safety checks, consider rollback if symptoms reappear.

sre-anna: ack, will monitor for next 6h and escalate if crash rate increases. setting alert thresholds tighter for the vllm pool.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-032 created and linked to CS-4921. severity set to P1 (customer impact). next update deadline 2026-03-15T03:15:00Z. :white_check_mark:
